entries.effect: one item of the document's /Outlines tree, which PDF 1.7 Table 8.2 makes a LINKED structure: the catalog names a root dictionary through /Outlines, every item names its /Parent, /Prev and /Next, and an item's children are its /First .. /Last chain.  Every member here is read by walking those links with the release's own dictionary and array readers, and the whole tree is reached through -[PDFDocument outlineRoot].  The children are built once and memoised because both -numberOfChildren and -childAtIndex: walk the same chain.  -insertChild:atIndex: and -removeFromParent are NOT implemented and their rows say why

entries.effect: the item at that position, nil for an index past the last child.  THE HOST RAISES THERE: -[PDFOutline childAtIndex:] with an index past the end throws NSRangeException, "childAtIndex: 2 out of bounds", measured.  That is a named boundary and not a match - a differential cannot compare a raised exception against an answer, so the harness does not ask one past the end, and a caller that gets nil can say so where a caller that gets an exception cannot

entries.effect: the one member whose rule is not the format's.  Table 8.2 says a POSITIVE /Count means the item is CLOSED; the host reads it the other way round - outline-signs.pdf has two items of the same shape, two children each, one with /Count +4 and one with /Count -4, and the positive one answers YES and the negative one NO.  And an item with NO /Count answers YES only when it has no /Title either: outline-titlekey.pdf's five leaves differ only in their /Title - none present, an empty /Title (), a real one - and only the first answers YES; outline-untitled.pdf's chain of four UNTITLED items answers NO, NO, NO, YES where outline-titled.pdf's chain of four TITLED items with the same shape answers NO four times; and the item's /F and /Dest make no difference.  So: YES when the /Count is positive, and YES when there is no /Count AND no /Title
